passage: Norse mythological texts derive from many sources, such as the Prose Edda, composed in the early 13th century, and the Volsunga Saga from the late 13th century. One of the most significant sources, Snorri Sturluson's Heimskringla, was written in the 1220s; some material from it was later adapted by the Icelandic poet Sturla Þórðarson into the Hákonar Saga in 1264. But Sturla didn't merely adapt Heimskringla, he added to it as well, introducing the famous concept of the eternal winter (fimbulwinter) as a precursor to Ragnarök, which suggests that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: Hákonar Saga is more mythologically comprehensive than Heimskringla, because the Volsunga Saga had not been written when Snorri Sturluson was composing his work.
choices.B: the Norse mythological traditions that the author of the Prose Edda drew on would not have featured the concept of fimbulwinter.
choices.C: Snorri Sturluson was unaware of stories of fimbulwinter when composing his Heimskringla, though scholars know that texts containing such stories were available to him.
choices.D: Snorri Sturluson's accounts of Norse mythology in his Heimskringla are more similar overall in content to the accounts in the Volsunga Saga than they are to the accounts in Hákonar Saga.

explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it most logically completes the discussion about the development of Norse mythological texts. The text establishes a chronology of Norse sources, with the Prose Edda composed in the early 13th century (the 1200s), Snorri Sturluson's Heimskringla written in the 1220s, Sturla's Hákonar Saga in 1264, and the Volsunga Saga in the late 13th century (1250–1300). Importantly, the text indicates that along with adapting Snorri's Heimskringla, Sturla added "the famous concept of the eternal winter (fimbulwinter)" to it. If Sturla introduced the idea of fimbulwinter in 1264, it logically follows that this concept was not present in earlier works. This suggests that the Norse mythological traditions that informed the Prose Edda, which was written before both Snorri's and Sturla's works, would not have featured the concept of fimbulwinter.
